newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Masood forces launch major attack on Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Masood forces launch major attack on Taleban.

text.p: Forces loyal to ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood launched a heavy attack on Wednesday on forces led by the Taleban Islamic militia, eyewitnesses said.
They said the attack, using rockets, artillery and infantry, was apparently aimed at taking the strategic heights above Kabul, the Afghan capital which the Taleban captured on September 27.
From Kalakan, which is about 25 km (18 miles) north of Kabul, witnesses said they could see shells landing on Taleban positions.
"We are moving around to encircle them and we will move on Kabul, God willing," said Ustod Rahim, one of Masood's commanders.
The shelling was particularly heavy on the so-called new road which leads into northeastern Kabul.
Afghan forces arrayed against the fundamentalist Taleban militia began moving up armour and artillery on Tuesday in apparent preparation for an attempt to seize the heights above Kabul.
